Fufu: Ghana. Fufu (or fufuo, foofoo, foufou foo-foo) is a pounded meal found in West African cuisine.
Who is credited with discovering Tennessine?
Tennessine: Yuri Oganessian. Tennessine is a synthetic element; it has symbol Ts and atomic number 117.
Who is credited with discovering Ammonia?
Ammonia: Joseph Priestley. Ammonia is an inorganic chemical compound of nitrogen and hydrogen with the formula NH3.
Who is credited with discovering Selenium?
Selenium: Jöns Jacob Berzelius. Selenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Se and atomic number 34.
These large seabirds of the tubenose order range widely across the Southern Ocean and North Pacific, but are notably absent from the North Atlantic today. What birds are they?
Albatross are large seabirds related to the procellariids, storm petrels, and diving petrels in the order Procellariiformes (the tubenoses).
Closely related to Hepatica and Pulsatilla, which flowering plant genus in the buttercup family is nicknamed the windflower?
Anemone is a genus of flowering plants in the buttercup family Ranunculaceae.
With almost 500 species in the daisy family, this large plant genus includes mugwort, wormwood, and sagebrush, and is sometimes confused with a related genus of sages — which genus?
Artemisia (plant) (art--) is a large, diverse genus of plants belonging to the daisy family, Asteraceae, with almost 500 species.
Marketed early on as the Debonair in its conventional-tail form, this piston single has been built continuously longer than any other aircraft ever made — which model?
Beechcraft Bonanza is an American general aviation aircraft introduced in 1947 by Beech Aircraft Corporation of Wichita, Kansas.
Ranging from southern Canada down to Oaxaca, Mexico, this North American wild cat sports black bars on its forelegs and a short, bobbed tail. What animal is it?
Bobcat (Lynx rufus), also known as the wildcat, bay lynx, or red lynx, is one of the four extant species within the medium-sized wild cat genus Lynx.
This basic unit of digital information most often consists of eight bits, and is called an 'octet' in network protocol documents to avoid ambiguity. What is it?
Byte is a unit of digital information that most commonly consists of eight bits.
A flightless ratite native to the tropical forests of New Guinea and northeastern Australia, this large bird has three living species and lacks a keel on its breastbone — name the bird?
Cassowary (Tok) are flightless birds of the genus Casuarius, in the order Casuariiformes.

A long-term lung condition that makes breathing progressively harder due to damaged airways and lung tissue, this condition develops gradually and currently cannot be cured, though treatments and lifestyle changes help manage symptoms. What is this disease, commonly abbreviated?
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a long-term lung condition that makes it progressively harder to breathe.
This group of mostly evergreen, cone-bearing trees and shrubs reproduces via wind-pollination, with the seeds themselves also scattered by the wind — what plant group is it?
Conifer are a group of vascular plants and a subset of gymnosperms.
First created in 1994 and named for the German city where it was made, this synthetic element with atomic number 110 sits below platinum on the periodic table — what's it called?
Darmstadtium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Ds and atomic number 110.
Its name comes from the Ancient Greek for 'female dragon,' and this genus of roughly 200 tree and shrub species now also includes what was once classified as Sansevieria — which genus is it?
Dracaena (plant) is a genus of about 200-220 species of trees and woody shrubs.

Named for Latin words meaning 'within the cytoplasm' and 'little net,' this eukaryotic cell organelle handles protein folding and comes in rough and smooth varieties, forming an interconnected network of membrane-enclosed sacs — name this organelle?
Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is a part of a transportation system of the eukaryotic cell, and has many other important functions such as protein folding.
Home to seven living cat species, from the tiny black-footed cat to the jungle cat, and the wild ancestor line of the housecat, which genus of felines is this?
Felis is a genus of small and medium-sized cat species native to most of Africa and south of 60 latitude in Europe and Asia to Indochina.

Heterotrophs like animals, members of this kingdom eat by secreting enzymes into their surroundings, and they get around mainly by simply growing — except for the occasional flagellated spore drifting through air or water. What group is it?
Fungus (pl.: fungi or funguses) is any member of the group of eukaryotic organisms that includes yeasts, molds, as well as mushrooms.
The largest living primate, with arm spans reaching 2.6 metres, this equatorial-African great ape shares up to 99% of its DNA with humans — what is it?
Gorilla are large, primarily herbivorous, great apes that live in the tropical forests of equatorial Africa.
In their healthy state these vascular cushions in the anal canal actually help with stool control — it's only when they swell or inflame that they earn the nickname "piles." What are they?
Hemorrhoid (or haemorrhoids), also known as piles, are vascular structures in the anal canal.
Behaviorally and physically dog-like despite being closer kin to felines, this carnivoran's family is the fifth-smallest in its order with only four extant species — what is it?
Hyena (hi-; from Ancient Greek, haina) are feliform carnivoran mammals belonging to the family Hyaenidae (Latin).

Also known by the old names green vitriol and copperas, this heptahydrate salt dissolves in water to form a paramagnetic, octahedral aquo complex and is used medically to fight anemia — which compound is it?
Iron(II) sulfate (British) denotes a range of salts with the formula FeSO4xH2O.

Nicknamed 'Marvellous Merchiston,' this Scottish laird and mathematician popularised the decimal point and invented a set of calculating 'bones' — but he's best known for discovering what underlies the slide rule. Who was he?
John Napier (Latinized as Ioannes Neper; 1 February 1550 - 4 April 1617), nicknamed Marvellous Merchiston, was a Scottish landowner known as a mathematician, physicist and astronomer.

This genus of rod-shaped, gram-positive bacteria forms a significant part of the human microbiota in places like the digestive and genital tracts, and until a 2020 taxonomic overhaul included 261 distinct species — what's the genus?
Lactobacillus is a genus of gram-positive bacteria within the Lactobacillaceae family.
This ACE inhibitor can take up to four weeks for full effect and is also used to prevent kidney problems in people with diabetes — which medication?
Lisinopril is a medication belonging to the drug class of angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors and is used to treat hypertension (high blood pressure), heart failure, and heart attacks.
Recognizable by the male's iridescent green head, this widespread dabbling duck species has been introduced to countries from New Zealand to South Africa far beyond its native range — what is it?
Mallard (Anas platyrhynchos) is a dabbling duck that breeds throughout the temperate and subtropical Americas, Eurasia, and North Africa.
Nicknamed "quicksilver," this is the only metallic element that stays liquid at room temperature, and it's often mined as the red mineral cinnabar — which element is it?
Mercury (element) is a chemical element; it has symbol Hg and atomic number 80.
Its English name passed from Greek to Latin to Portuguese before landing in English in the early 1600s — which family of roughly 200 marine fish species boasts 16 genera?
Moray eel are a family of eels whose members are found worldwide.
First linked by a Michigan doctor to farm wives sickened by isolation, this Gilded Age diagnosis grouped together fatigue, headaches, and a depressed mood — what condition?
Neurasthenia (from Ancient Greek (neuron) 'nerve' and (asthens) 'weak') is a term that was first used as early as 1829 for a mechanical weakness of the nerves.
In this learning process, voluntary behaviors grow more frequent through reinforcement or fade through punishment and extinction — what is it called?
Operant conditioning is a learning process in which voluntary behaviors are modified by association with the addition (or removal) of reward or aversive stimuli.
A physician in this medical field — devoted to the study of disease and diagnosing it largely by analyzing tissue and cell samples — is called a pathologist. What is the field?
Pathology is the study of disease. The word pathology also refers to the study of disease in general, incorporating a wide range of biology research fields and medical practices.
This branch of linguistics is concerned with how speech sounds are physically produced, transmitted as sound waves, and perceived by listeners — name the field?
Phonetics is a branch of linguistics that mainly concerns the articulation, sound wave properties, and perception of speech sounds.
Born Joseph Ratzinger in Bavaria, this pontiff led the Catholic Church from 2005 until an unusual resignation in 2013, after which he adopted an 'emeritus' title — who was he?
Pope Benedict XVI (born Joseph Alois Ratzinger; 16 April 1927 - 31 December 2022) was the head of the Catholic Church and sovereign of Vatican City from 2005 until his resignation in 2013.
Found in nucleic acids as the building block behind adenine and guanine, this nitrogen-rich heterocyclic compound is the most common of its kind in nature — what is it?
Purine is a heterocyclic aromatic organic compound that consists of two rings (pyrimidine and imidazole) fused together.
Home to about 200 species — among them the plants we call currants and gooseberries — this genus is the sole member of its own plant family — which genus?
Ribes is a genus of approximately 200 known species of flowering plants, predominantly native to the temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere.

This volatile, colorless, and odorless nerve agent is so potent a chemical weapon that inhaling a lethal dose can cause death from respiratory paralysis within one to ten minutes — what's the compound called?
Sarin (NATO designation GB short for G-series, B) is an extremely toxic organophosphorus compound that has been often used as a chemical weapon due to its extreme potency as a nerve agent.

Built for the Marine Corps by adding a third engine and a seventh main rotor blade to an earlier heavy-lift helicopter, this aircraft entered service in 1981 and flies from Navy ships — which helicopter?
Sikorsky CH-53E Super Stallion is a heavy lift helicopter operated by the United States military.
Members of the family Sciuridae, whose closest living relatives are surprisingly the mountain beaver and dormice, these rodents are native to the Americas, Eurasia and Africa — what are they called?
Squirrel (z)) are members of the family Sciuridae (sih-, -dee), a family that includes small or medium-sized rodents.

A leguminous tree bearing edible brown pod-like fruits with sweet, tangy pulp, indigenous to tropical Africa and naturalized in Asia, its wood and seed oil have varied uses from cuisine to traditional medicine. What is this tree?
Tamarind (Tamarindus indica) is a leguminous tree bearing edible fruit that is indigenous to tropical Africa and naturalized in Asia.
The largest member of the genus Panthera and an apex predator of Asian forests, this big cat wears orange fur striped in mostly-vertical black — what is it?
Tiger (Panthera tigris) is a large cat and a member of the genus Panthera native to Asia.
Nicknamed carbamide, this is the simplest amide of carbamic acid: two amino groups joined by a single carbonyl, and the body's chief way of shedding nitrogen in urine. What compound is it?
Urea (because it is a diamide of carbonic acid), is an organic compound with chemical formula CO(NH2)2.
He co-developed the V-2 at Peenemünde — the first artificial object to cross the Kármán line into space — before bringing his rocketry to the United States; who was this engineer?
Wernher von Braun (23 March 1912 - 16 June 1977) was a German American aerospace engineer and space architect.
Named for its standard passenger capacity, this twin-engine turboprop regional airliner is assembled in Toulouse by a Franco-Italian manufacturer that is half-owned by Airbus — what aircraft is this?
ATR 72: Regional turboprop airliner. The ATR 72 is a twin-engine turboprop, short-haul regional airliner developed and produced in France and Italy by aircraft manufacturer ATR.
Sold as button, cremini, or portobello depending on its stage of maturity, this cultivated mushroom is grown in more than 70 countries — what species is it?
Agaricus bisporus: Species of fungus. Agaricus bisporus, commonly known as the cultivated mushroom, is a basidiomycete mushroom native to grasslands in Eurasia and North America.
Meaning 'different lizard' and first described in 1877 by Othniel Marsh, most fossils of this Late Jurassic predator come from North America's Morrison Formation — which dinosaur?
This Manchester physicist shared the 2010 Nobel Prize for his work on graphene — and is the only person to also hold an Ig Nobel, won for levitating a frog with magnetism. Who is he?
In this severe blood disorder, the bone marrow stops producing red cells, white cells and platelets alike, and about half of all cases have no known cause — what condition is it?
Aplastic anemia: Disease causing insufficient blood cells of all types.

Often called a 'collapsed lung' in casual speech, this condition is really the partial deflation of the lung's alveoli rather than fluid filling them, and shows up frequently on chest X-rays — what is it?
Atelectasis: Partial collapse of a lung causing reduced gas exchange.
The only mammals capable of true sustained flight, this group flies on long digits webbed with a thin membrane and makes up about 20% of all classified mammals — what are they?
Members of this warm-blooded class range from the 5.5 cm bee hummingbird to the 2.8 m ostrich, share toothless beaked jaws, and lay hard-shelled eggs — what are they?
Bird: Warm-blooded animals with wings and feathers.
This highly venomous snake in the Colubridae family, scientifically known as Dispholidus typus, is native to Sub-Saharan Africa — what is its common name?
One of the largest snake species on Earth, this Southeast Asian native became invasive in Florida after escaping the pet trade — which snake is this?
Burmese python: Species of large, nonvenomous snake.
Its Latin name means 'horned goat,' and it's often pictured as a half-goat, half-fish sea creature — which is the smallest constellation of the zodiac?
Capricornus: Zodiac constellation in the southern hemisphere.

Nicknamed the 'solar' web for its sunburst of radiating nerve fibers, this abdominal structure sits behind the stomach and in front of the diaphragm's crura, near where several major arteries branch off the aorta — what is it?
Celiac plexus: Complex network of nerves located in the upper abdomen.

Caused by a bacterium and often symptomless for weeks after exposure, this sexually transmitted infection can lead to pelvic inflammatory disease and infertility in women if untreated — which infection?
Chlamydia: Sexually transmitted bacterial infection. Chlamydia, or more specifically a chlamydia infection, is a sexually transmitted infection caused by the bacterium Chlamydia trachomatis.
Striking at the same hour every day for weeks at a time, usually around one eye, this excruciating neurological condition is considered one of the most painful known to medicine — what is it?
Cluster headache: Neurological disorder. The disease is considered among the most painful conditions known to medical science.
These wind-pollinated, cone-bearing evergreens dominated Earth's landscapes throughout the Mesozoic before flowering plants took over — what group of plants is this?
Conifer: Group of seed plants. As of 2025, 94 conifer species are listed as endangered and 30 as critically endangered.
Encompassing roadrunners, koels, and anis among its roughly 150 species, this widespread bird family favors trees but includes some ground-dwellers — what is it?
Cuckoo: Family of birds. The cuckoo family includes the common or European cuckoo, roadrunners, koels, malkohas, couas, coucals, and anis.
This biological process, powered by rhythmic muscle waves called peristalsis, expels solid waste from the digestive tract through the anus or cloaca — what is it?
Defecation: Expulsion of feces from the digestive tract.
Bred around 1890 by a Thuringian tax collector looking for a loyal guard dog, this sleek, high-alert German breed traditionally had its ears cropped and tail docked — which breed?
Dobermann: Black and tan dog breed from Germany.
Dubbed 'the father of immunology,' this English physician created the world's first vaccine using cowpox to fight a disease that once killed up to a fifth of city dwellers — who is he?
Native to French Polynesia but nicknamed 'devil's ivy' for staying green even in the dark, this hardy houseplant has become an invasive nuisance worldwide — what's its scientific name?

Famous for the male's song delivered while hovering 50 to 100 metres above open farmland, this streaked greyish-brown bird has been introduced to Australia, New Zealand, Canada and Hawaii — what is it?
Eurasian skylark: Species of bird. The Eurasian skylark (Alauda arvensis), commonly referred to in Europe as the lark, is a passerine bird in the lark family, Alaudidae.
This biological process is the fusion of two gametes to create a zygote, distinct from earlier steps like insemination or pollination that merely bring the gametes together — what is it called?
Fertilisation: Union of opposite-sex gametes in sexual reproduction to form a zygote.

A particle physicist who later turned cattle rancher and founded San Francisco's Exploratorium, he was blacklisted by McCarthyism partly for being a more famous physicist's younger brother — who was he?
Frank Oppenheimer: American particle physicist and science educator (1912–1985)
This scientific field measures Earth's precise shape, gravity, and orientation in space, underpinning satellite positioning systems and global mapping — which discipline?
Geodesy: Science of measuring the shape, orientation, and gravity of Earth.
This type of organ produces an organism's sex hormones and gametes — testicles in males, ovaries in females — what is it called?
Gonad: Gland that produces sex cells.

Caused by a retrovirus that attacks the immune system, this condition has no cure or vaccine — yet with antiretroviral treatment a person can now expect to live a normal life and die with the virus, not of it. What is it?
HIV/AIDS: Spectrum of conditions caused by HIV infection.
The only Saskatchewan-born Nobel laureate, this Canadian-born chemist won the 1983 prize for unraveling the mechanisms of electron-transfer reactions in metal complexes — who was he?

Galaxies recede from Earth at speeds proportional to their distance, a relationship credited to a 1929 paper — though the maths behind an expanding universe had already been derived in 1922 by Alexander Friedmann. What's this relationship called?
Hubble's law: Observation in physical cosmology.
Known as 'the father of modern optics,' this Islamic Golden Age scholar wrote the influential 'Book of Optics' and proved that vision begins in the eye, not by rays leaving it — who is he?
Ibn al-Haytham: Arab physicist, mathematician and astronomer (c. 965 – c. 1040)
This Russian physiologist won the 1904 Nobel Prize for his work on digestion, but is far better remembered for training dogs to salivate at a signal — who was he?
Building his first firearm at age 13 in his father's gun shop, this American designer earned 128 patents and pioneered the autoloading pistol — who is he?
This NMDA-receptor-blocking anesthetic induces a trance-like dissociative state while preserving breathing and raising blood pressure, and at lower doses treats resistant depression — which drug?
Known to some as Al-Kashi's theorem, this trigonometric rule relates a triangle's three side lengths to the cosine of one of its angles — what is it called?
Law of cosines: Generalization of Pythagorean theorem.
Instrumental in the discovery of nuclear fission, this Austrian-Swedish physicist fled Nazi Germany in 1938 after losing her post under the Nuremberg Laws — who is she?
This American biologist argued that cells with nuclei arose from symbiotic mergers of bacteria, and co-developed the Gaia hypothesis with James Lovelock — who was she?

Originally hoping to become an engineer, this Italian physician became one of the first women to graduate from medical school in Italy and later devised an influential educational philosophy — who is she?
Maria Montessori: Italian physician and educator (1870–1952)
Comprising 18 to 24 species that hybridize freely where their ranges overlap, this genus of the mint family thrives in wet, moist soils worldwide — what is it?
Mentha: Genus of flowering plants in the family Lamiaceae.
NATO nicknames it 'Foxhound,' and at roughly 3,000 km/h it's the fastest operational combat aircraft known — which interceptor, a Soviet successor to the MiG-25, is it?
Mikoyan MiG-31: Interceptor aircraft. The MiG-31 is the fastest known operational combat aircraft, with a top speed around 3,000 km/h (1,600 knots).
Grown to feed silkworms for commercial silk production, this fast-growing tree releases its pollen at more than half the speed of sound — which species?
Morus alba: Plant species in the fig family.
Divided in two by a central septum, this air-filled space sits behind the nose and forms the uppermost part of the respiratory system — what is it?
Nasal cavity: Large, air-filled space above and behind the nose in the middle of the face.
A catecholamine whose very name nods to the kidney, it acts as both a hormone and neurotransmitter and is called "noradrenaline" outside the US — what is it?
Norepinephrine: Catecholamine hormone and neurotransmitter. The general function of norepinephrine is to mobilize the brain and body for action.
Its Greek name means 'serpent-bearer,' and it's depicted as a man grasping a snake represented by a neighboring constellation — which constellation straddles the celestial equator?
Ophiuchus: Constellation straddling the celestial equator. Ophiuchus ( o-fee-YOO-kəs) is a large constellation straddling the celestial equator.
This butterfly was the first species to be given the common name now applied to its entire family, and is widespread across the Palearctic and North America — which species?
Papilio machaon: Species of insect. Papilio machaon, the Old World swallowtail, is a butterfly of the family Papilionidae.
In placental mammals, this is the region of the body between the anus and the genitals, running from the pubic bone to the tailbone, and is often considered an erogenous zone — what is it called?
Perineum: Region of the body between the genitals and anus. The perineum (pl.: perineums or perinea) in placental mammals is the space between the anus and the genitals.

This French polymath's five-volume 'Celestial Mechanics' recast Newtonian physics in the language of calculus, and he pioneered both a widely used integral transform and helped shape Bayesian probability — who is he?
This plant genus — whose members go by names like poplar, aspen, and cottonwood — includes the first tree species ever to have its complete genome sequenced, in 2006 — what genus is it?
Populus: Genus of plants. Populus is a genus of 25–30 species of deciduous flowering plants in the family Salicaceae, native to most of the Northern Hemisphere.
Flagged by the WHO as one of the greatest antibiotic-resistance threats to humans, this rod-shaped bacterium causes hospital infections like ventilator-associated pneumonia — which pathogen?
Pseudomonas aeruginosa: Species of bacterium. P. aeruginosa is able to selectively inhibit various antibiotics from penetrating its outer membrane and has high resistance to several antibiotics.
Named for the ragged look of its leaves, this genus of flowering plants causes up to half of all pollen-related allergy cases despite a genus name meaning 'food of the gods' — which plant?
Ragweed: Genus of plants. The name "ragweed" is derived from "ragged" + "weed," coming from the ragged appearance of the plant's leaves.
Also called vitamin B2, this nutrient forms two key coenzymes for energy metabolism, can be prescribed for corneal thinning, and taken orally may cut down migraines in adults — which vitamin is it?
Riboflavin: Vitamin, dietary supplement, and yellow food dye.

Nicknamed 'The Kite' (or perhaps 'The Dragon'), this Swedish supersonic fighter-interceptor's innovative double-delta wing traces back to 1948 and entered frontline service in March 1960 — which aircraft?
Saab 35 Draken: 1955 Swedish fighter aircraft. The full-scale production version entered service with frontline squadrons of the Swedish Air Force on 8 March 1960.

Named after a colourful terrestrial flower, this predatory marine cnidarian is typically a single polyp anchored to a hard surface — a tentacled relative of coral and jellyfish, but with no medusa stage. What is it?
Sea anemone: Marine animals of the order Actiniaria.
Sitting just below carbon in group 14 of the periodic table, this blue-grey, brittle semiconductor is essential to plants and dominates the world's transistors and solar cells — which element is it?
Silicon: Chemical element with atomic number 14 (Si)
Commonly grown as an easy-care houseplant that tolerates low light, this genus of about 60 tropical species is better known by the nickname 'peace lily' — what genus is it?
Spathiphyllum: Genus of plants. Certain species of Spathiphyllum are commonly known as spath or peace lilies.
Usually found in pairs and recognized as a leading cause of pneumonia since the late 19th century, which bacterium often lives harmlessly in the respiratory tracts of healthy carriers?
Streptococcus pneumoniae: Species of bacterium. Streptococcus pneumoniae, or pneumococcus, is a Gram-positive, spherical bacteria, alpha-hemolytic member of the genus Streptococcus.
Marketed under the brand name Flomax, this alpha-blocker medication treats enlarged prostate symptoms and helps ease the passage of kidney stones — which drug?
Tamsulosin: Medication. Tamsulosin, sold under the brand name Flomax among others, is a medication used to treat symptomatic benign prostatic hyperplasia and chronic prostatitis.
First unearthed in Mongolia's Gobi Desert in 1948, this Late Cretaceous giant is known mainly from claw bones over half a meter long, giving it a name meaning 'scythe lizard' — which dinosaur genus?
Therizinosaurus: Therizinosaurid genus from the Late Cretaceous period.

Famous for oversized, colorful bills nearly useless for excavation, these Neotropical birds nest in hollows dug by other animals and share an ecological niche with Africa and Asia's hornbills — what are they?
Toucan: Family of birds. The family includes five genera and over 40 different species.
Made from strained yogurt mixed with cucumber, garlic, and herbs like dill or mint, this cold Greek dip is a classic topping for souvlaki and gyros — what is it called?
Tzatziki: Cold cucumber–yogurt dip, soup, or sauce.

The northernmost marsupial on Earth, this cat-sized nocturnal opportunist is a familiar visitor to trash cans and compost piles across North America, and often ends up as roadkill due to its slow pace — what is it?
Virginia opossum: Species of North American marsupial.
Aboard Apollo 8, the first crewed mission to leave low Earth orbit, this astronaut snapped the iconic "Earthrise" photograph as the crew circled the Moon ten times — who took it?
William Anders: American astronaut and lunar explorer (1933–2024)
The symbol for seaborgium is Sg. Seaborgium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Sg and atomic number 106.
The symbol for lanthanum is La. Lanthanum is a chemical element; it has symbol La and atomic number 57.

Ryan O'Neal: Charles Patrick Ryan O'Neal (April 20, 1941 – December 8, 2023) was an American actor.

The Banshees of Inisherin (in-ih-SHERR-in) is a 2022 black tragicomedy film directed, written, and co-produced by Martin McDonagh.

Aftersun is a 2022 semi-autobiographical coming-of-age drama film written and directed by Charlotte Wells in her feature directorial debut.

In what year was Gone Girl first released?
Gone Girl is a 2014 American psychological thriller film directed by David Fincher and written by Gillian Flynn, based on her 2012 novel.

Predestination is a 2014 Australian science fiction thriller film written and directed by Michael and Peter Spierig.
In what year was The Social Network first released?
